evidence: Sen. Ep. 87.2: culcita in terrā jacet, ego in culcitā
Cato Agr. 5.5: utī suō quisque locō cubet
terms.comment: To go to bed is cubitum īre (Cato Agr. 5.5).

terms.gloss: lie down, stretch out (on the ground)
lie down (in bed or at table); take to one’s bed

phrases.latin: culcita in terrā jacet, ego in culcitā
phrases.english: the mattress lies on the ground, and I lie on the mattress

phrases.latin: locō herbidō ut quiēte et pābulō laetō reficeret bovēs et ipsum fessum viā prōcubuisse
phrases.english: that he lay down in a grassy spot, to rest the cattle and feed them on rich grass, being tired from the road himself

phrases.latin: prīmus cubitū surgat, postrēmus cubitum eat
phrases.english: let him be the first to get up and the last to go to bed
